title: Vice-Chancellor's International Excellence Scholarship
deadline_central_display: No single closing date - the award is reviewed monthly
deadline_note: Cut-offs for holding an Offer of Place to be awarded: 30 November (A trimester), 31 May (B trimester), 31 August (C trimester) and 31 October (H or X trimester).
application_cycle: Reviewed monthly; applications are tied to the trimester in which you receive your Offer of Place
status_note: The scholarship page is marked 'Accepting applications' and states 'This scholarship is for all areas of study and is reviewed monthly. The above closing date does not apply.'
tuition_coverage_note: The published value is 'Up to NZD$15,000 towards tuition fees'.
benefits: Up to NZD$15,000 towards tuition fees
Open to all areas of study
Reviewed monthly rather than against a single annual closing date
eligibility: International students applying for an undergraduate or postgraduate taught qualification
Students who have enrolled in a programme that is made up of at least 120 points in total
Students who have applied for admissions through the right application process
Students who have excellent academic achievement or clear aspirations to succeed
requirements: Read the scholarship regulations to be sure you are eligible
Apply for admissions to a qualification offered at the University of Waikato first
Applications are completed in the Scholarship tab of your applicant record in MyWaikato
Apply by the seasonal cut-off for the trimester in which you receive your Offer of Place
Upon being awarded, enrol in the qualification in your scholarship offer
coverage: Up to NZD$15,000 towards tuition fees
application_method: Apply for admissions to a Waikato qualification
Complete the Scholarship tab in your applicant record in MyWaikato
application_route: Admissions application first, then the Scholarship tab of your MyWaikato applicant record by the cut-off for your Offer of Place trimester.
description: The Vice-Chancellor's International Excellence Scholarship is open to all areas of study at the University of Waikato and is worth up to NZD$15,000 towards tuition fees.

verification.notes: Value, study level, eligibility, application process and the seasonal cut-offs were read directly from the University of Waikato scholarship page. Note that the page is also linked from the University of Waikato German Winter School programme, which describes this scholarship alongside an additional NZD$8,000 towards accommodation expenses for students of the winter school.

applicant_utility: The unusual thing about this scholarship is that it is not a one-off annual deadline - Waikato reviews applications monthly, so your eligibility is decided against the trimester in which you are made an offer. In practice that means you cannot apply before you apply for admission, and you should submit the Scholarship tab in MyWaikato as soon as your Offer of Place lands rather than waiting. The value is capped at NZD$15,000 towards tuition fees, which will not cover a full degree on its own, so treat it as a discount rather than full funding and keep a separate plan for living costs, which the award does not touch. Any discipline is eligible, including taught postgraduate study, so it is worth applying even if you are enrolling in a professional or conversion degree rather than a research programme.

title: Vice-Chancellor's Scholarship for International Students
deadline_central_display: No single date - closing dates are 10 December (offshore) and 15 August (onshore) for a February start; 30 April (offshore) for a July start
deadline_note: The page lists closing dates of 10 December for a February start (offshore students), 30 April for a July start (offshore students) and 15 August for a February start (onshore students). Check the page for the exact dates applying to the current year.
application_cycle: Closing dates published by intake: February start offshore 10 December, onshore 15 August; July start offshore 30 April
status_note: The University of Otago publishes this scholarship on its scholarships site together with its application periods and closing dates.
tuition_coverage_note: The University states 'This scholarship is payable only as a credit towards tuition fees' and 'The value of the scholarship is $10,000 with a one-year tenure'.
benefits: For students starting in semester 2, $5,000 is released as a tuition credit in semester 2 and the balance in semester 1 of the following year
eligibility: International students commencing any undergraduate programme
Students who enrolled/s start at Otago on the strength of an overseas secondary school or postgraduate qualification
Students must not have previously studied for the same degree level
Students must have applied to Otago with transcripts, evidence of English language proficiency and details of any other scholarship conferred on them
requirements: Apply to study at Otago with complete transcripts, English language evidence and details of other scholarships conferred
Onshore applicants apply through the online Entrance Scholarship application and complete the first stages of enrolment through eVision during 1 July to 15 August
Offshore applicants must agree in their eVision study application to be considered for international scholarships
Deferral of first application is not possible - students must apply in the round before commencing and then request a deferral
application_method: Onshore applicants: apply via the online Entrance Scholarship application in MyOtago and complete eVision enrolment between 1 July and 15 August
Offshore applicants: agree to be considered for international scholarships within the eVision study application
application_route: Offshore applicants indicate their interest inside the eVision study application; onshore applicants use the online Entrance Scholarship application and complete eVision enrolment from 1 July.
description: The Vice-Chancellor's Scholarship for International Students is worth $10,000 and is payable only as a credit towards tuition fees, with a one-year tenure.

verification.notes: Value, tenure, application routes, application periods and closing dates were read directly from the University of Otago scholarship page. The assignment's official_source_url returned HTTP 404; the live scholarship page listed under official_updates_url is the current source and was used instead. The page also states that students sponsored by their home Government or the New Zealand Government are not eligible for this scholarship and that students cannot hold another Otago Undergraduate Entrance Scholarship at the same time.

applicant_utility: This is Otago's standard first-year international scholarship, but note the restriction: if your home government or the New Zealand government sponsors you, you are not eligible, and you cannot hold it at the same time as another Otago Undergraduate Entrance Scholarship. The money is a tuition credit only, so it never reaches your bank account and does nothing for rent or flights. Timing matters more here than with many other awards - onshore applicants must complete both the online Entrance Scholarship application and the first stages of eVision enrolment between 1 July and 15 August for a February start, while offshore applicants only need to tick the scholarship box inside the eVision study application by 10 December. If you defer your first application you must request the deferral yourself, because the award cannot simply roll over to the next round.
